https://www.myjoyonline.com/trump-names-.body: President Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller, the architect of his hardline immigration policy, as his new chief of staff following historic losses in the US midterm elections. Miller replaces Susie Wiles, who submitted her resignation after Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress, delivering a blow to the prospects for Trump's agenda in his final two years in the White House. Speaking to reporters, Trump said Wiles had "done a very good job", but "we've got to make moves sometimes". Miller, a Trump loyalist and deputy chief of staff who served as a senior adviser during his first administration, is set to take on the new role on Monday.One of Trump's closest aides, Miller, 41, stuck by the president following his 2020 election defeat and followed Trump back into power last year. On X, Miller called Trump "the most transformative political leader in American History" who has "single-handedly saved America from those who would destroy it". He thanked Wiles for her years of devoted service to the president, country and for her friendship. "The mission now is more clear than ever: Fight with all of our soul to support our President and defend this magnificent Republic," he wrote. Wiles gave her resignation to Trump on Thursday night, a US official told CBS News, the BBC's media partner. Three sources told CBS she quit because of the election losses. Trump said in a statement that Wiles would be moved to the "Trump Political Operation". He told reporters that Miller "gets it, very good politically". Wiles said being on Trump's team was "the honor of a lifetime". "I'm so proud to have been a part of what we've accomplished together," she said. "While my role may be changing, my commitment to the President and the mission never will," she added. It was unclear if her deputies would remain at the White House. Wiles, 69, is seen as among the most powerful figures in the Trump administration and someone particularly close to the US president. Asked last month whether Wiles could be replaced soon, Trump said there was "zero chance". "Susie is here and she's gonna be here for a long time," he said. Wiles recently had cancer, announcing in September, six months after her diagnosis, that she was in remission. Wiles, 69, is seen as among the most powerful figures in the Trump administration and someone particularly close to the US president. Asked last month whether Wiles could be replaced soon, Trump said there was "zero chance". "Susie is here and she's gonna be here for a long time," he said. Wiles recently had cancer, announcing in September, six months after her diagnosis, that she was in remission. Wiles had planned to stay in her role until the end of the year or early next year, sources familiar with her thinking told CBS News. However, the president accelerated her departure, the sources said. Wiles is not the only Trump administration official to leave following this week's midterm elections, which have prompted a reckoning among Republicans about how to address voters' rebuke of Trump's agenda. Several Department of Justice (DOJ) officials who carried out some of Trump's top priorities have also resigned since Republicans' sweeping losses in Tuesday's midterm elections. Harmeet Dhillon, the chief of the civil rights division, which focused on non-citizen voting and eliminating diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) initiatives, stepped down on Thursday. She also put a greater focus on protecting gun owners' rights and adopted legal positions that opposed civil rights protections for transgender people. John Eisenberg, head of the department's National Security Division, who had also worked in Trump's first administration, investigated media leaks and led the division that redacted millions of pages of federal files related to convicted paedophile Jeffrey Epstein. Jason Reding Quiñones, a US attorney in Florida, was at the centre of Trump's efforts to use the DOJ to prosecute perceived political foes. He investigated earlier criminal probes into Trump's handling of classified documents after he left office in 2021 and his campaign's contacts with Russia in the 2016 election. Asked why he elevated Miller to chief of staff, Trump told reporters on Friday: "Stephen's been with me from the beginning. He gets it, very good politically ... and he's a very good manager. He'll do a great job." Democrats took to social media to criticise Miller as Trump's new pick, accusing the president of doubling down despite voters' anger with his party's agenda. Democratic Congressman Robert Garcia, who would lead the House Oversight Committee when the party takes control of the chamber, said he would continue to investigate Miller and his "misconduct". "Stephen Miller is the architect of the unconstitutional ICE raids that have terrorized our communities and kidnapped and killed American citizens and immigrant families," he said, referencing US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Democratic House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Miller was "a dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist who has American blood on his hands". "His presence in government should be eradicated like a malignant tumor," he said. Trump administration communications director Steven Cheung praised Miller. "There is no bigger advocate for the Trump agenda than Stephen, and he will help the Administration deliver on monumental victories for the rest of this historic second term," he said. Miller comes from an Ashkenazi Jewish family in Santa Monica, California. In high school, he developed a taste for politics and voiced controversial opinions. He attended Duke University in North Carolina and, in 2009, became an aide to ultra-conservative Alabama Senator Jeff Sessions, the first senator to endorse Trump. During this time, Miller developed his hardline immigration policies and worked to kill a bipartisan immigration reform bill. He joined Trump's presidential campaign in January 2016 and has been loyal since. Miller spearheaded Trump's use of executive orders to advance his agenda, staunchly defending the administration's use of executive power. He championed "zero-tolerance" family separations, drove policies behind travel bans during Trump's first term, advocated for third-country deportations and urged immigration officials to make up to 300 arrests a day. A staunch supporter of Israel, Miller has also been hawkish about the US and Israel's joint military action in Iran
https://www.myjoyonline.com/trump-names-.title_zh: 特朗普任命斯蒂芬·米勒为白宫新任幕僚长
https://www.myjoyonline.com/trump-names-.body_zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普在美国中期选举遭遇历史性惨败后，任命其强硬的移民政策设计师史蒂文·米勒为新任幕僚长。米勒将接替苏西·威尔斯；共和党失去对国会两院的控制后，威尔斯提交辞呈，令特朗普议程在其白宫最后两年的前景遭受打击。特朗普对记者表示，威尔斯“工作做得非常出色”，但“我们有时必须采取行动”。米勒是特朗普的忠实支持者，曾任副幕僚长，并在特朗普第一任期内担任高级顾问，定于周一就职新职。特朗普最亲近的幕僚之一、41岁的米勒，在特朗普2020年大选失利后仍坚定支持他，并随特朗普于去年重返权力中心。米勒在X上称特朗普是“美国历史上最具变革性的政治领袖”，称他“单枪匹马将美国从那些想要毁灭美国的人手中拯救出来”。他感谢威尔斯多年来对总统和国家的忠诚付出以及与她的友谊，并写道：“如今我们的使命比以往任何时候都更加明确：倾尽全部力量支持我们的总统，捍卫这个卓越的共和国。”美国官员告诉CBS新闻——该媒体是BBC的合作伙伴——威尔斯于周四晚间向特朗普递交辞呈。三名消息人士告诉CBS，她因选举失利而辞职。特朗普在一份声明中说，威尔斯将被调往“特朗普政治行动团队”。他对记者表示，米勒“在政治上非常懂行”。威尔斯称，加入特朗普团队是她“一生的荣幸”。她说：“我非常自豪能够参与我们共同取得的成就。虽然我的职务可能发生变化，但我对总统和使命的承诺永远不会改变。”目前尚不清楚她的副手是否将继续留在白宫。现年69岁的威尔斯被视为特朗普政府中最有权势的人物之一，也是与这位美国总统关系尤为密切的人士。上个月被问及威尔斯是否可能很快被替换时，特朗普表示“完全没有可能”。他说：“苏西会留在这里，她还会在这里待很久。”威尔斯近期曾患癌症，她在9月确诊六个月后宣布病情已经缓解。威尔斯曾计划继续担任现职至年底或明年初，知情人士告诉CBS新闻。然而，这些消息人士称，总统提前促成了她的离任。本周中期选举后，威尔斯并非唯一离任的特朗普政府官员；此次选举促使共和党开始认真检讨如何回应选民对其议程的否决。自周二共和党在中期选举中惨败以来，多名负责落实特朗普若干首要政策目标的司法部官员也已辞职。负责非公民投票以及取消多元化、公平与包容（DEI）倡议等工作的公民权利处处长哈米特·迪利昂于周四辞职。她还更加重视保护枪支拥有者的权利，并采纳反对为跨性别者提供民权保护的法律立场。司法部国家安全司司长约翰·艾森伯格也曾在特朗普第一任期内任职；该司负责调查媒体泄密事件，并领导删除了数百万页与已定罪儿童性侵害者杰弗里·爱泼斯坦有关的联邦档案。美国联邦检察官杰森·雷丁·基诺内斯来自佛罗里达州，是特朗普利用司法部起诉其认定政治对手行动的核心人物。他曾调查针对特朗普2021年离任后处理机密文件以及竞选团队在2016年选举中与俄罗斯接触的早期刑事调查。当被问及为何提拔米勒出任幕僚长时，特朗普周五对记者说：“史蒂文从一开始就跟着我。他非常懂政治……而且他是一位非常优秀的管理者。他会干得很出色。”民主党人转向社交媒体批评特朗普选择米勒担任新任幕僚长，指责总统无视选民对该党议程的愤怒，仍在坚持既定路线。民主党众议员罗伯特·加西亚表示，当该党接管众议院后，他将出任众议院监督委员会主席，并继续调查米勒及其“不当行为”。他说：“史蒂文·米勒是那些违宪的ICE突袭行动的设计者，这些行动恐吓我们的社区，绑架并杀害美国公民和移民家庭。”他提及了美国移民与海关执法局。民主党众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯称，米勒是“危险的仇外者和鲁莽的极端分子，双手沾满美国人的鲜血”。他说：“必须像切除恶性肿瘤一样，彻底清除他留在政府中的影响。”特朗普政府通信主任史蒂文·张赞扬米勒。他说：“在推动特朗普议程方面，没有人比史蒂文更积极，他将在这一历史性第二任期剩余时间里帮助政府取得非凡胜利。”米勒出身于加利福尼亚州圣莫尼卡的一个阿什肯纳兹犹太家庭。读高中时，他培养了对政治的兴趣，并表达过一些有争议的观点。他就读于北卡罗来纳州杜克大学，2009年成为极端保守派阿拉巴马州参议员杰夫·塞申斯的助手；塞申斯是首位支持特朗普的参议员。在此期间，米勒形成了其强硬的移民政策，并致力于否决一项两党共同支持的移民改革法案。他于2016年1月加入特朗普总统竞选团队，此后一直忠心耿耿。米勒牵头推动特朗普利用行政命令推进其议程，并坚决为政府使用行政权力辩护。他力挺“零容忍”家庭分离政策，推动特朗普第一任期内的旅行禁令背后的政策，主张将移民驱逐至第三国，并敦促移民官员每天实施多达300次逮捕。作为以色列的坚定支持者，米勒还支持美国和以色列在伊朗采取联合军事行动，并一贯持强硬立场……

https://www.myjoyonline.com/why-the-us-m.summary: That's the question which is hanging over investors, and which has prompted steep falls on the world's stock markets. https://www.myjoyonline.com/why-the-us-m.summary_zh: 这个问题一直悬在投资者心头，并促使全球股市大幅下跌。特斯拉老板曾花费近4.5亿美元支持共和党在中期选举中的竞选活动。英国科技公司Arm Holdings联合创始人Tudor Brown指出：“股票价值取决于未来收益，而非当前收益”。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/why-the-us-m.body: Is the artificial intelligence (AI) gold rush coming to an end, or is this simply a reality check? That's the question which is hanging over investors, and which has prompted steep falls on the world's stock markets. The sell-off in the US on Thursday was most dramatic on the Nasdaq, home to tech industry titans such as Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta and Apple. It followed sweeping gains by the Democrats in this week's midterm elections in the US, which have given the party full control of Congress. A number of leading Democrats campaigned against the unhindered expansion of data centres, which have underpinned the growth of artificial intelligence. Fears this will lead to more regulation of AI appear to have concerned investors. But worries about the industry's prospects have been growing for some time. The release of Chat GPT by Open AI in late 2022 is widely seen as having generated massive public and corporate interest in the practical uses of AI. It also sparked a modern-day gold rush. Investors flocked to put their money into companies producing computer chips and networking infrastructure, building data centres and providing the energy to power them, as well as developing the AI itself. The value of tech companies soared. The boom continued into this year. Investments in AI are expected to reach $1trillion in 2026 alone according to research by Goldman Sachs. The sector has scooped up so much available cash that other industries have seen their own borrowing costs increase as a result. But investors want returns, and in recent months concerns have been growing about whether the AI boom can produce the expected riches. Those worries have emerged at a time when public comments from AI researchers casting doubt over the safety of artificial intelligence - even suggesting it could represent an existential threat to humanity - have been grabbing headlines and fuelling speculation that a clampdown could lie ahead. While the Trump administration has been all-in on AI, or "super intelligence" as the president likes to call it, many leading Democrats tapped into grassroots concerns about the expansion of data centres and their impact on local communities. These were largely focused on the facilities' high consumption of water and electricity, which many feared would push up their household bills – as well as the noise, use of land, and general disruption associated with them. A Gallup poll published in May showed 71% of Americans would oppose the building of a data centre in their community. The figure for a nuclear power station was 53%. James Talarico, who won the Senate race in once staunchly Republican Texas, was one of those to respond to this scepticism. "While we want to protect America's leadership in artificial intelligence, we are still grappling with how it will affect everything from how we work to how our children learn," he said. "We must protect Americans and establish clear, consistent laws for businesses." With control of both houses of Congress, Democrats are now expected to challenge the president's technology agenda more vigorously, while introducing legislation which could curb the expansion of the industry. Texas' Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned against data centres, pledging a moratorium on the construction of new facilities. Hinojosa's win could present opposition to tech multi-billionaire Elon Musk, who has moved large parts of SpaceX and Tesla's operations to the state, for years a Republican stronghold. The Tesla boss had spent nearly $450m to back Republican campaigns in the midterms. As the co-founder of the British-based technology firm Arm Holdings, Tudor Brown, points out, "stock values are based on future earnings not present earnings". If the rewards are not likely to be as great as expected, some investors will choose to sell up. The falls seen on stock markets over the past 24 hours would appear to have been triggered by the midterm results. But concerns that tech firms have become overvalued were being expressed long before the elections. The question now is whether this is simply the removal of froth from an over-exuberant market, or a sign that the AI rush is a bubble about to burst, with much wider consequences. Nandini Roy Choudhury of Future Market Insights thinks investors will assess whether the political shift could result in restrictions on data centre construction, energy consumption and the deployment of AI technology. She adds there is unlikely to be an immediate widespread recovery in tech stocks as traders are likely to be more selective, favouring firms with stronger balance sheets. Brown thinks the impact will be limited. Share valuations, he thinks, were inflated by expectations of "almost infinite AI growth", which have been followed by "a bit of a panic". "There is a natural floor to this", he says. "After that it will reflect I think that actually there's still a lot of money being made in these companies"
https://www.myjoyonline.com/why-the-us-m.title_zh: 美国中期选举为何引发人工智能股票抛售
https://www.myjoyonline.com/why-the-us-m.body_zh: 人工智能（AI）淘金热是否即将结束，还是说这只是一次现实检验？这个问题悬在投资者心头，并促使全球股市大幅下挫。周四美国股市的抛售在纳斯达克最为显著，该指数是 Alphabet、Nvidia、Meta 和 Apple 等科技行业巨头的所在地。此前，民主党在美国本周的中期选举中取得全面胜利，使该党完全掌控国会。多名民主党领军人物曾 campaigned 反对无节制扩张数据中心，而数据中心一直是推动人工智能发展的基础。投资者似乎担心中共将导致人工智能受到更多监管。然而，有关该行业前景的担忧已经升温一段时间。Open AI 于2022年末推出 Chat GPT，被普遍视为激发了公众和企业对人工智能实际应用的巨大兴趣，也引发了现代版淘金热。投资者纷纷将资金投入生产计算机芯片和网络基础设施、建设数据中心并为这些设施提供能源的公司，也投入开发人工智能本身的企业。科技公司的市值飙升。这一热潮延续到了今年。据 Goldman Sachs 研究，仅2026年人工智能投资额预计就将达到1万亿美元。该行业吸收了大量可用现金，以至于其他行业的借贷成本也随之上升。但投资者希望获得回报，近几个月来，他们越来越担心中共热潮能否带来预期中的巨额财富。这些担忧出现之际，AI研究人员公开质疑人工智能的安全性，甚至暗示它可能对人类构成生存性威胁，相关言论频频登上头条，并引发市场猜测未来可能实施更严格的管制。特朗普政府对人工智能全力推进，或者说用总统喜欢的话来说，是推进所谓“超级智能”，但许多民主党领军人物则抓住了基层民众对数据中心扩张及其对当地社区影响的担忧。这些担忧主要集中于这些设施大量消耗水和电力，许多人担心这会推高家庭账单，同时还涉及噪声、土地占用以及相关设施带来的普遍干扰。Gallup 今年5月发布的民调显示，71%的美国人反对在本社区建设数据中心，而针对核电站的这一比例为53%。曾在共和党据点得克萨斯州赢得参议院选举的 James Talarico 是回应这种疑虑的人士之一。他说：“在希望保护美国人工智能领导地位的同时，我们仍在努力解决它将如何影响从我们的工作方式到孩子学习方式的一切。我们必须保护美国人，并为企业制定明确、一致的法律。”在掌控国会两院后，民主党如今预计将更积极地挑战总统的技术议程，同时提出可能遏制该行业扩张的立法。得克萨斯州当选民主党州长 Gina Hinojosa 反对建设数据中心，承诺暂停新设施施工。Hinojosa 的胜选可能会给科技业亿万富翁 Elon Musk 带来阻力。多年来，得克萨斯州一直是共和党 stronghold，而 Musk 已将 SpaceX 和 Tesla 的大部分业务迁至该州。这位 Tesla 负责人曾花费近4.5亿美元支持共和党的中期选举竞选活动。英国科技公司 Arm Holdings 联合创始人 Tudor Brown 指出：“股票价值取决于未来收益，而非当前收益。”如果回报不太可能达到预期水平，一些投资者就会选择卖出。过去24小时股市出现的下跌，看起来是由中期选举结果触发的。但认为科技企业估值过高的担忧，在选举前很久就已出现。现在的问题是：这仅仅是在剔除过度亢奋市场中的泡沫，还是表明人工智能淘金热是一个即将破裂的泡沫，并将带来更广泛的影响？Future Market Insights 的 Nandini Roy Choudhury 认为，投资者将评估政治格局的变化是否可能导致数据中心建设、能源消费和人工智能技术部署受到限制。她补充称，科技股不太可能立即全面反弹，因为交易员很可能会更加挑剔，青睐资产负债表更稳健的企业。Brown 认为，影响将十分有限。他认为，股价因“近乎无限的人工智能增长”预期而被推高，随后又出现了“一阵恐慌”。“这自然存在一个底部，”他说，“此后我认为股价会反映出，这些公司实际上仍在赚取大量资金。”

https://www.myjoyonline.com/afenyo-marki.body: Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin is pushing for the Minister of Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, to appear before the House to explain the shutdown of Ghana’s Health Information Management Systems. Mr Afenyo-Markin wants the Minister to brief Parliament on the circumstances that led to the disruption of the systems, reportedly following an unpaid cloud hosting bill of more than US$64,000. The issue was raised in Parliament amid concerns about the impact of the disruption on health information management and reporting across the country. Responding to the call, the Majority Leader, James Agalga, assured the House that steps would be taken to invite Mr Akandoh to explain the circumstances surrounding the shutdown. He said the engagement would also provide an opportunity for Parliament to examine the challenges and establish measures to ensure the affected systems are restored. The shutdown, which took effect on October 29, 2026, followed the suspension of 10 servers by technology provider Akamai over an outstanding payment of US$64,510.95, according to information from the Ghana Health Service. Among the affected platforms is the District Health Information Management System (DHIMS2), which supports the collection, analysis and reporting of health data across the country. Other affected platforms include the Planning and Budget Management Information System, eTracker, HIV and tuberculosis trackers, and the National Malaria Data Repository. The disruption has forced health facilities to temporarily rely on paper-based records while the Ghana Health Service works to restore access to the systems. The Service has indicated that settling the outstanding hosting bill could allow the suspended platforms to be restored without rebuilding them

https://www.myjoyonline.com/afenyo-marki.body_zh: 少数派领袖亚历山大·阿芬约-马金正推动卫生部长夸贝纳·明塔·阿坎多到议会出席，说明加纳卫生信息管理系统为何停运。阿芬约-马金希望部长向议会汇报导致这些系统中断的情况。据报道，中断源于一笔超过64,000美元的云托管费未予支付。此事在议会提出之际，各方担忧系统中断将影响全国卫生信息管理和报告工作。针对这一要求，多数派领袖詹姆斯·阿加尔加向议会保证，将采取行动邀请阿坎多先生说明停运的相关情况。他说，有关沟通还将让议会有机会审查相关挑战，并制定措施，确保恢复受影响的系统。据加纳卫生署提供的信息，此次停运自2026年10月29日起生效。此前，技术供应商Akamai因一笔64,510.95美元的欠款，暂停了10台服务器。受影响的平台包括支持全国卫生数据收集、分析和报告的地区卫生信息管理系统（DHIMS2）。其他受影响的平台还有规划与预算管理信息系统、eTracker、艾滋病和结核病追踪系统以及国家疟疾数据储存库。中断已迫使各医疗机构暂时依靠纸质记录，同时加纳卫生署正着手恢复对相关系统的访问。该署表示，缴清拖欠的托管费用后，便可恢复被暂停的平台，而无须重新构建它们

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.body: Timor-Leste President Jose Ramos-Horta, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate, received this year’s Internet Peace Prize at the National Assembly on Friday. The Sunfull Foundation, chaired by Chung-Ang University professor and anti-cyberbullying activist Min Byoung-chul, jointly hosted the event with the Assembly’s Sunfull Committee at Sarangjae, a hanok-style event space on the grounds of the National Assembly. Lawmakers, foreign ambassadors and people who worked on Sunfull's most recent campaign against artificial intelligence (AI) deepfakes attended. “I hope this event will deepen friendship and cooperation between Korea and Timor-Leste and foster greater international effort to create a peaceful and safe digital environment,” Rep. Song Seok-jun, chairman of the Assembly's Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee, said. The award honors individuals or organizations that help curb malicious online speech while advancing human rights and world peace, according to the foundation. Ramos-Horta shared the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize for his efforts to secure a peaceful resolution to the conflict in Timor-Leste. The ceremony followed the foundation’s September declaration against harmful AI-created deepfakes and malicious online comments, which brought together lawmakers, diplomatic representatives from 13 countries, teachers and students to call for greater protection of human dignity online. The foundation highlighted growing international efforts to address deepfake-related harm, citing legislative and regulatory measures in Korea, the United States and Europe. “Protecting people’s dignity from AI deepfakes and hateful online comments is a bipartisan responsibility,” said Rep. Lee Jeong-heon, co-chair of the Assembly’s Sunfull Committee. “The National Assembly will work to ensure that the Sunfull movement’s efforts to promote digital peace are firmly embedded in policy.” “President Ramos-Horta’s decision to forgive those who tried to assassinate him shows the way forward for digital peace in the AI era,” Min said. “I hope the 2026 Internet Peace Prize will resonate deeply in a world rife with abusive language and hate speech, offering a valuable lesson for our times.”
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.title_zh: 东帝汶总统Ramos-Horta赢得2026年互联网和平奖
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/lifestyle/p.body_zh: 东帝汶总统、诺贝尔和平奖得主何塞·拉莫斯-奥尔塔周五在国民议会领取了今年的网络和平奖。活动在全国议会 grounds 内一座韩屋风格的活动空间Sarangjae举行，由Sunfull Foundation与国民议会的Sunfull Committee共同主办。Sunfull Foundation主席、梨花女子大学教授兼反网络霸凌活动家Min Byoung-chul主持了活动。议员、外国使节以及参与Sunfull最近一次反人工智能（AI）深度伪造运动的人士出席了活动。国民议会外交与统一委员会主席宋锡俊议员表示：“我希望这次活动能够加深韩国与东帝汶之间的友谊与合作，并推动国际社会更加努力地营造和平安全的数字环境。”据该基金会介绍，该奖项表彰在促进人权和世界和平的同时，帮助遏制恶意网络言论的个人或组织。拉莫斯-奥尔塔因推动以和平方式解决东帝汶冲突，曾分享1996年诺贝尔和平奖。颁奖仪式之前，该基金会于9月发表了反对有害AI生成深度伪造和恶意网络评论的宣言，汇集议员、来自13个国家的外交代表、教师和学生，共同呼吁加强网络空间的人权尊严保护。该基金会强调，国际社会正日益努力应对深度伪造带来的危害，并列举了韩国、美国和欧洲采取的立法与监管措施。国民议会Sunfull Committee联席主席李正宪议员说：“保护人的尊严，使其免受AI深度伪造和仇恨网络评论侵害，是两党共同的责任。”“国民议会将努力确保Sunfull运动推动数字和平的努力切实融入政策。”Min表示：“拉莫斯-奥尔塔总统决定宽恕那些曾企图暗杀他的人，为人工智能时代的数字和平指明了前进方向。”“我希望2026年网络和平奖能够在充斥辱骂语言和仇恨言论的世界中引起深刻共鸣，为我们这个时代提供宝贵启示。”

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body: Gold investment has drawn renewed interest in Korea as international bullion prices rebound while domestic stocks sold off sharply following the Democrats’ capture of both chambers of Congress in the U.S. midterm elections. The election outcome raised expectations that Congress could curb President Donald Trump’s plans to expand fiscal spending, putting downward pressure on U.S. Treasury yields and the dollar. Lower yields make gold, which pays no interest, more attractive, while a weaker dollar makes it cheaper for buyers using other currencies. The domestic spot price of gold closed at 176,690 won ($130) per gram Friday, according to the Korea Exchange. Although slightly lower than the previous session, it remained 4.53 percent above its Nov. 2 level. The modest decline followed a 2.64 percent gain Thursday, when gold finished at 178,460 won per gram, up 5.58 percent from Nov. 2. In contrast, KOSPI and Kosdaq fell 6.02 percent and 5.03 percent, respectively, Friday, extending Thursday’s losses of 5.28 percent and 5.11 percent. Retail prices also climbed. A don of pure gold, a traditional Korean unit equivalent to 3.75 grams, cost 777,000 won, up from 730,000 won on Oct. 31. Overseas, spot gold was trading at $4,129.16 per ounce on Thursday, up more than 6 percent for the week and on track for its biggest weekly gain since August. “Precious metals staged a sharp recovery from their year lows as the election results put pressure on the dollar and Treasury yields,” said Ok Ji-hoe, an analyst at Samsung Futures, adding that the prospect of political gridlock could limit new fiscal spending, further reducing the cost of holding nonyielding assets like gold. The domestic stock market sell-off may have further increased gold’s appeal. Fears of tighter regulation of artificial intelligence data centers weighed on major semiconductor stocks, potentially encouraging investors to seek traditional havens. Citi has set a short-term price target of $4,500 an ounce, suggesting further upside. Still, it remains to be seen whether the latest recovery can hold. Gold and silver surged last year as investors sought protection from market uncertainty, but lost ground this year amid rising interest rates and concerns about tighter monetary conditions. Despite the recent bounce, gold remains down more than 6 percent since the start of the year
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.title_zh: 美国中期选举后韩国股市暴跌，黄金重新受到关注
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body_zh: 随着国际金银价格反弹，以及民主党在美国中期选举中赢得国会参众两院后韩国国内股市大幅下挫，黄金投资重新受到关注。选举结果提高了市场对国会能够遏制美国总统唐纳德·特朗普扩大财政支出计划的预期，从而对美国国债收益率和美元形成下行压力。较低的收益率提高了不孳息的黄金的吸引力，而美元走弱则降低了使用其他货币的买家购买黄金的成本。据韩国交易所（Korea Exchange）数据，周五韩国国内黄金现货价格收于每克176,690韩元（$130）。这一价格虽略低于前一交易日，但仍较11月2日高出4.53%。金价小幅下跌此前曾于周四上涨2.64%，当日黄金收于每克178,460韩元，较11月2日上涨5.58%。相比之下，韩国综合股价指数（KOSPI）和韩国科斯达克指数（Kosdaq）周五分别下跌6.02%和5.03%，延续了周四分别下跌5.28%和5.11%的跌势。零售价格也上涨了。一套纯金首饰价格达到777,000韩元，高于10月31日的730,000韩元；一套纯金首饰是韩国的传统计量单位，相当于3.75克。海外方面，周四现货黄金报每盎司$4,129.16，周涨幅超过6%，有望录得8月以来的最大单周涨幅。Samsung Futures分析师Ok Ji-hoe表示：“随着选举结果对美元和国债收益率形成压力，贵金属从年内低点大幅反弹。”他还说，政治僵局的前景可能限制新的财政支出，进一步降低持有黄金等无收益资产的成本。国内股市的抛售可能进一步提升了黄金的吸引力。市场担心人工智能数据中心将面临更严格的监管，这拖累了主要半导体股，可能促使投资者转向传统避险资产。花旗已将黄金短期目标价定为每盎司$4,500，这意味着金价仍有进一步上涨空间。不过，最新一轮反弹能否持续仍有待观察。去年，在投资者寻求对冲市场不确定性之际，黄金和白银价格飙升，但今年受利率上升及货币条件趋紧担忧影响，两者均出现下跌。尽管近期有所反弹，黄金较年初仍下跌逾6%

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body: Um Woo-chong, a veteran international administrator and former senior official at the Asian Development Bank, has been appointed the inaugural head of the World Bank Group's new accountability mechanism, making him only the second Korean to reach the vice-president level at the global institution, the Ministry of Finance and Economy said Friday. The World Bank Group’s boards of directors named Um on Wednesday as vice president and director general of the Independent Accountability Mechanism. He will take office on Jan. 18. The mechanism handles grievances from communities harmed, or at risk of being harmed, by projects the group finances, and independently reviews whether those projects meet environmental and social standards. Its chief is appointed directly by the boards and operates independently of management. The body merges three existing complaint channels — the World Bank’s Inspection Panel and Dispute Resolution Service, which is the ombudsman office serving the International Finance Corporation, along with the group’s private-sector lending arm and the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, which provides political risk insurance to investors. Um has more than 30 years of experience in international development finance. He joined the Manila-based ADB in 1993 and served as its director general for sustainable development and climate change before becoming managing director general, the post coordinating key initiatives across the bank, from 2021 to 2024. He has since been CEO of the Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet, a nonprofit founded in New York in 2021. His appointment follows that of Kim Sang-bu, named the World Bank’s vice president for digital and artificial intelligence in July 2024. In May, Min Jeen-ah became the group’s director of market and counterparty risk. The ministry said it expects the appointments to raise Korea’s standing in international financial institutions. It plans to keep supporting Koreans seeking such posts through recruitment briefings and programs under which the government funds young professionals to work at the institutions for two years. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.title_zh: 亚洲开发银行前官员Um Woo-chong获任世界银行集团副总裁
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/economy/202.body_zh: 韩国财政部周五表示，资深国际事务管理人员、亚洲开发银行前高级官员吴宇钟获任世界银行集团新问责机制首任负责人，成为第二名在該全球机构担任副总裁级别的韩国人。世界银行集团董事会周三任命吴宇钟为独立问责机制副总裁兼总干事。他将于1月18日就职。该机制负责受理受到该集团资助项目损害或可能受损社区的申诉，并独立审查这些项目是否符合环境和社会标准。其负责人由董事会直接任命，独立于管理层运作。该机构将现有三个申诉渠道合并，包括世界银行监察小组、担任国际金融公司监察专员办公室的争议解决服务，以及该集团私营部门贷款机构和提供投资者政治风险保险的多边投资担保机构。吴宇钟拥有30多年的国际发展融资经验。他于1993年加入总部位于马尼拉的亚洲开发银行，曾任可持续发展与气候变化总干事，之后于2021年至2024年担任管理总干事，负责协调该行各项重点倡议。此后，他担任全球能源联盟为人民与地球首席执行官；该非营利组织于2021年在纽约成立。他的任命紧随金相武之后，后者于2024年7月被任命为世界银行数字与人工智能副总裁。今年5月，闵贞娥出任该集团市场与交易对手风险负责人。财政部表示，预计这些任命将提升韩国在国际金融机构中的地位。该部计划通过招聘说明会和政府资助年轻专业人士到相关机构工作两年的项目，继续支持争取此类职位的韩国人。本文在生成式人工智能协助下完成，并由《韩国时报》编辑。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.summary: Seeks deliberate investment in domestic digital infrastructure, stronger regulatory institutions Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has cautioned that Nigeria should not allow a repeat of the decàdes-long mistakes it made in managing its oil economy in the burgeoning digital sector.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.summary_zh: 大力投资国内数字基础设施、强化监管机构。财政部长兼经济协调部长Taiwo Oyedele警告称，在蓬勃发展的数字经济领域，尼日利亚不应重蹈其数十年来管理石油经济时犯下的错误。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.body: Seeks deliberate investment in domestic digital infrastructure, stronger regulatory institutions Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has cautioned that Nigeria should not allow a repeat of the decàdes-long mistakes it made in managing its oil economy in the burgeoning digital sector. He recalled that exporting crude oil and importing refined petroleum products deprived Nigeria of substantial domestic value, expertise and employment opportunities, stressing that the country must not allow a similar pattern to emerge in the digital ecosystem. The minister maintained that the scale of the opportunity was already evident, citing figures by the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) showing that Nigeria had more than 157 million active internet subscriptions as at May 2026. However, he pointed out an estimate by the Nigeria Data Protection Commission showing that over 90 per cent of the country’s data is hosted abroad. The minister explained that digital sovereignty entails a country’s ability to determine, under its own laws, how its data is collected, stored, accessed and utilised, clarifying that this did not mean shutting Nigeria out of the global digital economy, but ensuring that its participation advances national interests. To reverse the trend, he called for deliberate investment in domestic digital infrastructure, stronger regulatory institutions and the development of local expertise and businesses capable of converting data into valuable products and services within Nigeria. On Artificial Intelligence (AI), Oyedele highlighted its growing capacity to reshape employment and the skills required in the emerging economy, and charged graduates to embrace AI and other emerging technologies while retaining their independent judgement, critical thinking, creativity, empathy and integrity. He also enjoined young Nigerians to be deliberate about their conduct in the digital space, noting that their online footprints increasingly influence their personal and professional identities. Their posts, comments and reactions, he noted, could shape how employers, institutions and society perceive them. The minister counselled graduates to disagree respectfully, challenge ideas rather than attack individuals, and understand that online attention does not necessarily translate into respect, popularity into credibility or virality into value creation. He also drew attention to the capacity of AI to amplify misinformation, impersonation and dishonesty, making ethical conduct and public trust increasingly important. Turning to the role of universities, Oyedele charged higher institutions to move beyond the traditional award of certificates and position themselves as centres of innovation, entrepreneurship, ethical leadership and practical problem-solving. He argued that their relevance should also be measured by the problems their graduates solve, the businesses they establish and the contributions they make to their communities. Oyedele identified agriculture, energy, healthcare, marine resources, environmental management and digital services as sectors offering significant opportunities for innovation and enterprise, calling on universities to equip students with the practical knowledge and skills to develop solutions in these areas. He outlined five responsibilities for the graduating students, including lifelong learning, value creation, integrity, responsible digital citizenship and active participation in nation-building. The minister explained that Nigeria’s digital future would depend not only on technology and infrastructure, but also on the values, choices and capabilities of the people shaping its development. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.title_zh: 奥耶德莱警告勿在数字经济领域重犯石油经济时代的错误
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/11/06/o.body_zh:
财政部长兼经济协调部长泰沃·奥耶德莱警告，尼日利亚不应在蓬勃发展的数字经济领域重蹈过去数十年在管理石油经济时所犯的错误。他回顾称，出口原油并进口成品油使尼日利亚损失了大量国内价值、专业知识和就业机会，强调国家必须防止类似模式在数字生态系统中出现。

这位部长表示，机会的规模已经显而易见。他援引尼日利亚通信委员会（NCC）的数据称，截至2026年5月，尼日利亚的活跃互联网订阅数已超过1.57亿。然而，他指出，尼日利亚数据保护委员会的一项估计显示，该国90%以上的数据托管在海外。

部长解释道，数字主权意味着一个国家能够依据本国法律决定其数据的收集、存储、访问和利用方式。他澄清，这并不意味着将尼日利亚排除在全球数字经济之外，而是要确保其参与全球数字经济能够推进国家利益。为扭转这一趋势，他呼吁有针对性地投资国内数字基础设施、强化监管机构，并培养本地专业人才和发展企业，使它们能够在尼日利亚国内将数据转化为有价值的产品和服务。

谈及人工智能（AI），奥耶德莱强调，人工智能日益具备重塑就业形态以及新经济所需技能的能力，并要求毕业生拥抱人工智能和其他新兴技术，同时保持独立判断力、批判性思维、创造力、同理心和正直品格。他还告诫尼日利亚年轻人，在数字空间活动时应审慎行事，因为其网络足迹正日益影响个人和职业身份。他指出，年轻人发布的帖子、评论和互动可能影响雇主、机构和社会对他们的看法。

这位部长建议毕业生以尊重的方式提出异议，对观点提出挑战而非攻击个人，并认识到网络关注度不一定会转化为尊重，人气也不一定会转化为公信力，病毒式传播更不意味着创造价值。他还提醒人们关注人工智能放大错误信息、冒名行为和不诚实现象的能力，这使得道德行为和公众信任变得日益重要。

在谈及高校的作用时，奥耶德莱要求高校超越传统颁发证书的职能，将自身定位为创新、创业、道德领导力和实际问题解决的中心。他认为，高校的相关性还应体现在其毕业生所解决的问题、所创办的企业以及对所在社区所作的贡献上。

奥耶德莱指出，农业、能源、医疗保健、海洋资源、环境管理和数字服务等领域为创新和创业提供了重大机会，并呼吁高校培养学生实用的知识和技能，使他们能够针对这些领域开发解决方案。他为即将毕业的学生提出了五项责任，包括终身学习、创造价值、保持正直、负责任地参与数字公民活动以及积极参加国家建设。

部长解释道，尼日利亚的数字未来不仅取决于技术和基础设施，也取决于塑造其发展进程的国民所秉持的价值观、所作的选择和所具备的能力。

https://leadership.ng/adc-ruling-aa-pres.summary: The AA presidential candidate, in a statement on Friday, November 6, 2026, described the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) under former Senate President David Mark and invalidating the presidential nomination of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as troubling.
https://leadership.ng/adc-ruling-aa-pres.summary_zh: 该党总统候选人在2026年11月6日星期五发表的声明中称，联邦高等法院裁定非洲民主大会（ADC）由前参议院议长戴维·马克领导的领导层无效，并使前副总统阿提库·阿布巴卡尔的总统提名无效，此举令人不安。
https://leadership.ng/adc-ruling-aa-pres.body: He cautioned that the development could set a dangerous precedent for opposition politics, insisting that every political party and candidate had a stake in protecting democratic participation and the people’s right to choose their leaders. The AA presidential candidate, in a statement on Friday, November 6, 2026, described the Federal High Court judgment nullifying the leadership of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) under former Senate President David Mark and invalidating the presidential nomination of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar as troubling. He said the timing of the judgment, barely two and a half months before the 2027 general elections, had raised serious questions about judicial independence, political competition and the future of Nigeria’s democracy. Fadojoe stressed that his reaction was not based on party affiliation, noting that he was not a member of the ADC but believed that an injustice against democratic participation in one party could threaten the rights of other opposition candidates. On the role of the judiciary, Fadojoe acknowledged the importance of the courts in upholding the Constitution and ensuring that political actors operate within the law. “Why has Nigeria become a country where political parties spend more time defending their existence in courtrooms than presenting solutions to the Nigerian people?” he queried. He also questioned why elections were increasingly becoming entangled in prolonged litigation, factional disputes and last-minute judicial pronouncements. The AA presidential candidate maintained that no political party or candidate should be above the law, but insisted that judicial decisions must take into account their broader implications for democratic participation. Fadojoe consequently called for urgent measures to restore public confidence in the independence, consistency and impartiality of the Nigerian judicial system. He urged President Tinubu and the APC to recognise that Nigerians were closely monitoring developments within the country’s political landscape. He maintained that the survival of Nigeria’s democracy depended on protecting political plurality, strengthening democratic institutions and ensuring that voters, rather than institutional controversies, ultimately determined the country’s political leadership. https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.title: Key lessons Korea should learn from US midterm elections
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.summary: Trump has been checked, not finished The U.S. midterm elections have delivered a decisive setback to President Donald Trump and the Republican Party. For Korea, the message is straightforward: Do not mistake a midterm election for the end of Trump or the Republican Party. The midterm elections demonstrate that American voters can hold their leaders accountable.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.summary_zh: 特朗普受挫，但尚未出局。美国中期选举给唐纳德·特朗普总统和共和党带来了决定性的挫折。对韩国而言，信息很明确：不要把中期选举误认为特朗普或共和党的末日。中期选举表明，美国选民能够追究其领导人的责任。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.body: Trump has been checked, not finished The U.S. midterm elections have delivered a decisive setback to President Donald Trump and the Republican Party. Democrats have captured both the House of Representatives and the Senate, fundamentally changing the political landscape in Washington. Yet the significance of this defeat should not be exaggerated. Trump has suffered a serious political setback, not a political death sentence. The Republican Party has lost control of Congress but remains a powerful political force. For Korea, misunderstanding this distinction could have serious consequences. Three issues contributed substantially to the Republican defeat: the war with Iran, concerns about corruption and the continuing struggle of ordinary Americans to afford everyday necessities. The Iran war has become a major political liability. However, dissatisfaction with the war should not automatically be interpreted as opposition to its strategic objectives. Some Americans recognize Iran as a serious security threat but question the administration's execution, costs and strategy for ending the conflict. Others oppose the war itself. As a former soldier, I believe military action must be judged not only by its justification but also by its objectives, execution and political consequences. Winning battles does not necessarily produce strategic success. Affordability has also influenced voters. Housing, food, energy, health care and declining purchasing power affect everyday life. Regardless of Washington's economic explanations, Americans judge their government by what they experience. Corruption represents another serious concern. Allegations involving conflicts of interest, personal enrichment and political favoritism have raised questions about accountability. Particularly troubling is the perceived scale, blatancy and apparent normalization of questionable conduct. Not every allegation constitutes proven wrongdoing, but the perception that political leaders operate under different rules is damaging. Nevertheless, Koreans should understand that Republican rejection does not mean Democratic endorsement. Many Americans voted against the administration's performance rather than out of renewed confidence in Democratic leadership. One encouraging development is that America's constitutional system continues to function. Trump has acknowledged the election results and indicated a willingness to work with Democrats, although confrontation is inevitable. His acceptance of the outcome is important, even if genuine cooperation remains uncertain. The incoming Democratic Congress will possess considerable investigative and legislative authority. Hearings, investigations, budget confrontations and challenges to executive decisions are likely. Impeachment may become part of the political debate, but removing a president requires a two-thirds Senate majority, making conviction difficult without substantial Republican support. Legislative stalemate appears more likely than dramatic political transformation. However, political deadlock does not necessarily mean democratic failure. America's constitutional system deliberately divides authority to prevent excessive concentrations of power. The coming confrontation will test whether political leaders respect those boundaries. How Washington conducts and concludes its Iran operations will provide important lessons for America's allies and adversaries alike. Iranian leaders may interpret the Democratic victory as evidence that Trump is politically finished and American pressure will diminish. That would be a dangerous miscalculation. Trump retains substantial presidential authority, particularly in foreign affairs and national security. Congressional opposition may complicate military policy, but it does not automatically prevent further action. Indeed, political setbacks sometimes encourage leaders to demonstrate resolve. This does not mean Trump will necessarily escalate the conflict. Nevertheless, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps could remain a potential American military target. Tehran should also recognize that American concerns about Iran extend beyond Trump and the Republican Party. Mistaking political division for strategic paralysis could prove costly. For Korea, the message is straightforward: Do not mistake a midterm election for the end of Trump or the Republican Party. Korean politicians, commentators and policymakers should resist the temptation to celebrate Republican losses or ridicule the U.S. president. Such behavior would be strategically shortsighted. More importantly, Koreans must remember that the U.S. is home to millions of decent, hardworking, patriotic citizens who are deeply proud of their country. They may disagree bitterly over politics, but their patriotism deserves respect. Criticizing a U.S. president is one thing. Insulting the American people is quite another. Koreans should also examine their own political shortcomings. Our country has experienced corruption, polarization, political scandals and abuses of power. We are hardly qualified to lecture Americans about the imperfections of democracy. There is a Korean proverb about a dog covered in filth criticizing another dog for having a little dirt on its coat. Americans have a similar expression: "People who live in glass houses should not throw stones." Before pointing fingers at Washington, Koreans should examine their own political conduct. We must also remember that these decent Americans are the people whose fathers, mothers, sons and daughters served, fought and died alongside Koreans defending our freedom. Their sacrifices deserve respect regardless of political affiliation. Temporary political disagreements must never become expressions of national arrogance or ingratitude. The Korea-U.S. alliance is not a relationship between one Korean administration and one U.S. political party. It is a partnership between two nations whose security and prosperity remain closely connected. Seoul must therefore maintain productive relationships with the Trump administration, Democratic congressional leaders and influential Republicans. This is especially important as both countries confront North Korea's nuclear threat, defense burden-sharing, wartime operational control transition and military modernization. Koreans are entitled to personal opinions about American politics. However, public officials and influential figures must distinguish between personal preferences and statements that could damage national interests. The midterm elections demonstrate that American voters can hold their leaders accountable. They also show that military decisions, economic hardship and concerns about government integrity carry electoral consequences. But America's political divisions have not disappeared. They have entered a new institutional environment. For Korea, the appropriate response is neither celebration nor alarm. It is strategic patience, diplomatic discipline, humility and respect for the American people. The Republican Party has been defeated, but it has not disappeared. Above all, Americans deserve our respect. Alliances must remain stronger than the political fortunes of individual leaders. In diplomacy, knowing when to keep one's opinions to oneself can be just as important as knowing what to say. Chun In-bum is the former commander of the Republic of Korea Army Special Warfare Command
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.title_zh: 韩国应从美国中期选举中汲取的重要经验
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/202.body_zh: 特朗普受挫，但尚未出局。美国中期选举给唐纳德·特朗普总统和共和党带来决定性挫折。民主党赢得了众议院和参议院的控制权，从根本上改变了华盛顿的政治格局。然而，不应夸大这次失败的意义。特朗普遭遇的是严重的政治挫折，而不是政治死刑。共和党失去了对国会的控制，但仍是强大的政治力量。对韩国而言，误解这一区别可能造成严重后果。三个问题促成了共和党的败选：与伊朗的战争、腐败问题，以及普通美国人继续难以负担日常生活必需品。对这场战争的不满，已成为一个重大政治负担。然而，不应自动把对战争的不满解读为反对其战略目标。一些美国人承认伊朗构成严重安全威胁，但质疑政府在结束冲突时的执行方式、成本和战略。另一些人则反对战争本身。作为一名前军人，我认为，军事行动不仅要以其理由是否正当来衡量，还要看其目标、执行方式和政治后果。赢得战斗并不一定能带来战略成功。可负担性也影响了选民的投票。住房、食品、能源、医疗保健和购买力下降都会影响日常生活。无论华盛顿如何解释经济状况，美国人都会根据自身经历来评判政府。腐败是另一个严重关切。涉及利益冲突、个人牟利和政治偏袒的指控，引发了人们对问责机制的质疑。尤其令人不安的是，这种不当行为的规模、公开程度，以及似乎已趋于正常化的状态，并非每项指控都能构成经证实的不法行为，但认为政治领导人遵守不同规则的观感会造成损害。尽管如此，韩国人应明白，共和党落选并不意味着民主党获得背书。许多美国人投票是为了反对本届政府的表现，而不是出于重新看好民主党领导层。一个令人鼓舞的进展是，美国的宪政体系仍在发挥作用。特朗普承认了选举结果，并表示愿意与民主党合作，尽管冲突不可避免。他接受选举结果十分重要，即便真正合作的前景仍不确定。即将上任的民主党国会将拥有相当大的调查和立法权。听证、调查、预算博弈以及对行政决定的挑战都很可能出现。弹劾可能成为政治辩论的一部分，但罢免总统需要参议院三分之二多数，因此在缺少大量共和党支持的情况下，很难定罪。立法僵局似乎比剧烈的政治转型更有可能出现。然而，政治僵局并不一定意味着民主失败。美国的宪政体系有意分权，以防止权力过度集中。即将到来的对抗将考验政治领导人是否尊重这些边界。华盛顿如何实施并结束对伊朗的行动，将为美国的盟友和对手 alike 提供重要启示。伊朗领导人可能把民主党的胜利解读为特朗普在政治上已经出局、美国施压将减弱的证据。那将是危险的误判。特朗普仍掌握相当大的总统权力，尤其是在外交事务和国家安全方面。国会的反对可能使军事政策复杂化，但不会自动阻止进一步行动。事实上，政治挫折有时会促使领导人展示决心。这并不意味着特朗普必然会升级冲突。尽管如此，伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队仍可能成为美国潜在的军事目标。德黑兰也应认识到，美国对伊朗的关切不局限于特朗普和共和党。把政治分歧误判为战略瘫痪，可能会付出代价。对韩国而言，信息很明确：不要把中期选举误认为特朗普或共和党的末日。韩国政界人士、评论人士和政策制定者应抵制庆祝共和党败选或嘲笑美国总统的诱惑。这种做法在战略上是短视的。更重要的是，韩国人必须记住，美国是数百万正直、勤奋、爱国公民的家园，他们为自己的国家深感自豪。他们可能在政治问题上激烈分歧，但他们的爱国精神值得尊重。批评美国总统是一回事，侮辱美国人民则完全是另一回事。韩国人也应审视自身的政治缺陷。我们的国家经历过腐败、政治极化、政治丑闻和滥用权力。我们 hardly 有资格就民主的不完美来教训美国人。韩国有句谚语，说一条满身污泥的狗嘲笑另一条狗的外套上沾了一点土。美国也有类似的说法：“住在玻璃房子里的人不应扔石头。”在指责华盛顿之前，韩国人应先审视自己的政治行为。我们还必须记住，这些正直的美国人的父亲、母亲、儿子和女儿曾与韩国人并肩服役、战斗并牺牲，保卫我们的自由。无论政治立场如何，他们的牺牲都值得尊重。暂时的政治分歧绝不能变成民族傲慢或忘恩负义的表现。韓美同盟不是韩国一个政府与美国一个政党之间的关系，而是两个安全与繁荣紧密相连的国家之间的伙伴关系。因此，首尔必须与特朗普政府、民主党国会领导人以及有影响力的共和党人维持富有成效的关系。这一点尤其重要，因为两国都在应对朝鲜核威胁、防务负担分担、战时作战指挥权移交和军事现代化。韩国人可以对美国政治持个人意见。然而，公职人员和有影响力的人物必须区分个人偏好与可能损害国家利益的言论。中期选举表明，美国选民能够追究领导人的责任，也显示军事决策、经济困境和政府对廉洁的关切都会带来选举后果。但美国的政治分歧并未消失，而是进入了一种新的制度环境。对韩国而言，适当的回应既不是庆祝，也不是惊慌，而是战略耐心、外交纪律、谦逊和尊重美国人民。共和党已经败选，但并未消失。最重要的是，美国人民值得我们的尊重。联盟必须比个别领导人的政治命运更加牢固。在外交中，知道何时把意见留给自己，可能与知道该说什么同样重要。辛仁范是韩国陆军特战司令部前司令。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.summary: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.summary_zh: 代表埃多州北区的参议员亚当斯·奥肖莫霍勒表示，联邦政府批准每月发放₦70,000交通津贴，体现出总统博拉·蒂努布对劳动者福祉的关切。奥肖莫霍勒周四接受《Channels Television》的《今日政治》节目采访时发表上述言论，并为蒂努布政府的施政表现辩护，同时敦促尼日利亚人珍惜政府的各项政策。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.body: Senator representing Edo North, Adams Oshiomhole, has said President Bola Tinubu has demonstrated concern for workers’ welfare through the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance. Oshiomhole made the statement during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s performance and urged Nigerians to appreciate its policies. “I think this government is doing well. If a man who was on ₦70,000 now is given ₦70,000 addition that makes it ₦140,000 for him it’s a hundred percent increase and if you know what ₦10,000 means for the real masses, you’ll appreciate that Tinubu has shown that he cares,” he said. The Federal Government approved the monthly ₦70,000 transport intervention for workers across all levels for six months, beginning in November 2026, following a meeting with the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) on October 27. The agreement also provides for the payment of outstanding peculiar allowances in three equal monthly instalments beginning in November. However, the Trade Union Congress (TUC) rejected the transport allowance, insisting that workers need a permanent salary increase rather than temporary relief. Oshiomhole also criticised the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which Atiku Abubakar served as vice-president, alleging that it failed to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. He said the 2027 presidential election would offer Nigerians a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whom he accused of allowing multiple exchange rates that favoured people based on their connections. The senator also faulted the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, for allegedly failing to present an alternative to Tinubu’s policies. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” Oshiomhole said. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.title_zh: 蒂努布以₦70,000津贴表明自己关心工人
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/11/tinu.body_zh: 代表埃多州北区的参议员亚当斯·奥希奥莫霍尔表示，联邦政府批准每月向劳动者发放₦70,000交通补贴，说明总统博拉·蒂努布切实关注劳动者福祉。奥希奥莫霍尔周四在Channels Television的《今日政治》节目中接受采访时作出上述表态。他为蒂努布政府的表现辩护，并敦促尼日利亚民众 appreciate 其政策。他说：“我认为本届政府表现良好。如果一个人原本领取₦70,000，如今又获得₦70,000，那么他的收入就是₦140,000，增幅达到100%。如果你明白₦10,000对普通民众意味着什么，你就会体会到蒂努布确实表示了关切。”联邦政府在10月27日与尼日利亚劳工大会（NLC）会晤后，批准从2026年11月起，为各级劳动者提供为期六个月的每月₦70,000交通补贴。协议还规定，从11月开始，分三个月的等额 installments 支付拖欠的特殊津贴。然而，尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）拒绝接受交通补贴方案，坚持认为劳动者需要永久性加薪，而不是临时救济。奥希奥莫霍尔还批评了奥卢塞贡·奥巴桑乔前总统执政时期，指出阿蒂库·阿布巴卡尔曾任该政府副总统，并声称政府未能确保按时支付劳动者工资。他说，2027年总统选举将让尼日利亚民众在蒂努布和阿蒂库之间作出选择；他认为蒂努布实现了统一汇率，而阿蒂库则纵容多种汇率并存，使有关系的人从中受益。这位参议员还指责尼日利亚民主党（NDC）总统候选人彼得·奥比，称其未能提出取代蒂努布政策的替代方案。奥希奥莫霍尔说：“彼得·奥比没有提出任何替代方案。我一直说彼得·奥比是个商人；商人的逻辑是短期周转。蒂努布所代表的是政治家式的思维，他会考虑下一代。”奥希奥莫霍尔说。本文所表达的观点不代表Vanguard newspapers及其任何员工的意见

https://leadership.ng/unilorin-unveils-2.title: UNILORIN Unveils 200-hectare Science Park To Attract Chinese Investors
https://leadership.ng/unilorin-unveils-2.summary: The University of Ilorin (UNILORIN) has unveiled plans to develop a 200-hectare Science, Technology and Innovation Park in Kwara State as part of efforts to attract Chinese investors, promote technology transfer and accelerate Nigeria’s industrial development.
https://leadership.ng/unilorin-unveils-2.summary_zh: 伊洛林大学（UNILORIN）公布了在夸拉州建设一座占地200公顷的科学、技术与创新园的计划，旨在吸引中国投资者、推动技术转让并加快尼日利亚的工业发展。
https://leadership.ng/unilorin-unveils-2.body: The University of Ilorin (UNILORIN) has unveiled plans to develop a 200-hectare Science, Technology and Innovation Park in Kwara State as part of efforts to attract Chinese investors, promote technology transfer and accelerate Nigeria’s industrial development. The vice-chancellor of the university, Prof. Wahab Egbewole, disclosed this at the NACCIMA B2B Investment Matchmaking Exchange 3.0 in Guangzhou, China, where he presented the project to more than 200 Chinese investors. Egbewole said the proposed park would provide an integrated ecosystem for academic research, industrial production, technological innovation and private-sector investment, creating opportunities for manufacturing, agriculture and Information and Communication Technology (ICT). He called for stronger collaboration between universities and the private sector, particularly in research commercialisation, technology transfer, industrial development and investment, noting that partnerships between educational institutions and businesses were critical to unlocking Nigeria’s economic potential. The event attracted key Nigerian and Chinese stakeholders, including the National President of the Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture (NACCIMA), Engr. Jani Ibrahim; Nigeria’s Consul-General in Guangzhou, Ambassador Mairo Musa Abbas; and Vice-President of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), Huang Xiaofeng. The university’s investment proposal attracted considerable interest from participants, particularly the 200-hectare Science, Technology and Innovation Park, which is designed to bring research institutions, technology companies, start-ups and industrial investors into a common business and innovation environment. According to details published by Innovation Report, UNILORIN is developing supporting infrastructure, including roads, water and electricity, to facilitate the establishment and operation of businesses within the proposed park. The project will leverage the university’s existing research capabilities, including approximately 52 patents, its laboratories, more than 70,000 students and a large pool of academic expertise. The initiative is expected to provide Chinese investors and manufacturers with opportunities to establish production facilities, research centres, technology incubation hubs and joint ventures in Nigeria, while benefiting from the university’s research and technical capabilities. The proposed park also aligns with efforts to strengthen the relationship between academia and industry by translating research findings into commercially viable products, services and industrial solutions. Speaking at the investment forum, Egbewole emphasised the need for Nigeria to move beyond its traditional position as an import-dependent economy and become a competitive destination for manufacturing, technology investment and industrial production. China’s industrial development experience, he noted, offers important lessons for Nigeria, particularly in building productive capacity, strengthening local industries and promoting research-driven enterprises. The broader objective of the NACCIMA B2B engagement was to connect Nigerian businesses and institutions with credible Chinese investors capable of providing capital, technical expertise and strategic partnerships to support economic development. Through its trade and investment facilitation initiatives, NACCIMA is seeking to promote opportunities that will encourage foreign investors to establish businesses, transfer technology and develop sustainable partnerships with Nigerian institutions and enterprises. The UNILORIN Science, Technology and Innovation Park is expected to contribute to these efforts by positioning the university as a potential destination for industrial investment and research commercialisation. The initiative also aligns with Nigeria’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy by 2030, with industrial parks, manufacturing hubs and export-oriented investments expected to play significant roles in expanding productive capacity and driving economic growth. https://leadership.ng/unilorin-unveils-2.title_zh: 伊洛林大学 unveils 200公顷科技园，吸引中国投资者
https://leadership.ng/unilorin-unveils-2.body_zh: 伊洛林大学（UNILORIN）宣布计划在夸拉州开发一座占地200公顷的科技与创新园，作为吸引中国投资者、促进技术转让并加速尼日利亚工业发展的一部分。该校校长瓦哈卜·埃格沃勒教授在中国广州举行的NACCIMA B2B投资对接交流活动3.0上披露了这一计划，并向200多名中国投资者介绍该项目。埃格沃勒表示，拟议中的创新园将打造一个涵盖学术研究、工业生产、技术创新和私人部门投资的综合生态系统，为制造业、农业以及信息通信技术（ICT）创造机遇。他呼吁加强大学与私营部门之间的合作，尤其是在研究成果商业化、技术转让、工业发展和投资等方面，并指出教育机构与企业之间的合作对于释放尼日利亚经济潜力至关重要。活动吸引了尼日利亚和中国的重要利益相关方，包括尼日利亚商会、工业、矿业与农业协会（NACCIMA）全国主席、工程师贾尼·易卜拉欣；尼日利亚驻广州总领事迈罗·穆萨·阿巴斯大使；以及中国国际贸易促进委员会（CCPIT）副主席黄小峰。该大学的投资方案引起了与会者的浓厚兴趣，尤其是占地200公顷的科技与创新园。该园旨在将研究机构、科技企业、初创企业和产业投资者汇聚于统一的商业与创新发展环境。根据Innovation Report公布的细节，伊洛林大学正在建设配套基础设施，包括道路、供水和供电设施，以促进拟议园区内企业的设立和运营。该项目将利用该大学现有的研究能力，包括约52项专利、实验室、超过7万名学生以及大批学术专家。该计划预计将为中国投资者和制造商提供在尼日利亚设立生产设施研究中心、技术孵化中心和合资企业的机会，同时使其能够利用该大学的研究与技术能力。拟议中的创新园还将呼应加强学术界与工业界联系的努力，将研究成果转化为具有商业可行性的产品、服务和产业解决方案。在投资论坛上，埃格沃勒强调，尼日利亚需要摆脱传统上依赖进口的经济模式，成为制造业、技术投资和工业生产具有竞争力的目的地。他指出，中国工业发展的经验为尼日利亚提供了重要启示，特别是在建设生产能力、 strengthening local industries and promoting research-driven enterprises。NACCIMA开展B2B活动的总体目标，是将尼日利亚企业和机构与具备提供资本、技术专长及战略合作能力的中国投资者对接，以支持经济发展。通过贸易和投资促进举措，NACCIMA寻求创造机遇，鼓励外国投资者在尼日利亚设立企业、转让技术，并与尼日利亚各机构和企业建立可持续的合作伙伴关系。伊洛林大学科技与创新园预计将通过将该大学定位为产业投资和研究商业化的潜在目的地，为这些努力作出贡献。该计划也符合尼日利亚到2030年打造1万亿美元经济的雄心，届时工业园、制造业中心和出口导向型投资预计将在扩大生产能力、推动经济增长方面发挥重要作用。掌握先机。获取实时报道、独家内幕和独家视角，直接传送至您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时随地接收全天候最新消息 →

https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.summary: The midterm results just re-echoed Stoken’s point that the pendulum of US politics swings toward the middle all the time, not despite the voters, but because of them. https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.summary_zh: 中期选举结果再次印证了斯托肯的观点：美国政治的钟摆始终朝向中间路线，不是因为选民而偏离中间路线，而是正因为选民才会如此。然而，由于民主党通过建立保姆型国家、层层增加繁文缛节并将 wokeism 奉为圭臬而迷失方向，特朗普的特立独行看起来便像是中间路线。仍待观察的是，中期选举是否终于让特朗普白宫吸取教训，而这一教训它此前在试图颠覆世界时未能学会。
https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.body: The midterm results just re-echoed Stoken’s point that the pendulum of US politics swings toward the middle all the time, not despite the voters, but because of them. One Trump term (2017-2021) was enough. But because the Democratic Party had lost its way by creating a nanny state, compounding red tape, and deifying wokeism, Trump’s idiosyncrasies looked like middle ground. He was voted in again in 2024, despite his hubris. Two years later, the pendulum is swinging left again. It’s funny that a president who dragged the US into a needless Middle East war with serious economic consequences for the world, sparked global tariff wars, criminalised migration, and bullied neighbours and allies alike is unable to save his party from electoral ruin. Voters have just reminded him that all 45 presidents who have occupied the White House since 1776 are tenants, not owner-occupiers. If it were up to him, Trump would have stuffed the ballots, created a crisis, or manufactured any subterfuge to change the results. But despite his disdain for process, his vindictive narrow-mindedness and desperation for vengeance, he could not. Despairing voters tamed him on November 3. Americans, or at least a significant number of them, have delivered the first nationwide verdict on Trump’s second term. Midterms are not a presidential election, but this one almost assumed the character of one – with President Barack Obama and Trump himself hitting the road and mounting the soapbox. The outcome is a Democratic breakthrough that feels like a landslide. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives were on the ballot, along with 35 of the 100 Senate seats and 36 governorships. The stakes were straightforward: Republicans controlled both chambers of Congress. Following the polls, Democrats flipped the hitherto red Congress to blue. The contest itself was not merely between two parties. It was between two versions of America – one energised by Trump’s MAGA delusions; the other alarmed by the cost of living, Trump’s misuse and abuse of power, and the slow unravelling of the American dream. As an unwritten rule, midterm elections often punish the president’s party. Voters, having handed a president the keys to the White House, return two years later to endorse or denounce the state of affairs. And since Trump-2 happened, the state of affairs has been not just perilous but life-threatening. With Americans being shot on the streets by ICE agents in what is clearly state-sanctioned murder, and vindictive attacks on critics like Ilhan Omar, the election assumed unusual urgency. Trump himself led the Republican campaigns, asking voters to assume he was on the ballot. That was a clear indication that, despite his incorrigibility, he was troubled by a likely unfavourable verdict – which is what he got. He told Americans to pretend he was on the ballot (he recanted after the devastating defeat), and offered a generous $5,000 bribe for every vote if Republicans won. His oligarch, Elon Musk, reportedly spent $474 million. Yet, Trump was punished, and Republicans lost. His approval rating has been near record lows, with public dissatisfaction focused on the economy and a foolish war in Iran, which a Republican Congress never felt any urgency about but felt helpless to stop. The election results are proof that Trump has been a liability and a political misadventure at the White House, as Republican candidates struggled to distance themselves from a president who demands loyalty and rarely admits error. They were still Trump enablers, and their loss should not be mourned. For Democrats, the election has been a breath of fresh air, and an opportunity to rebuild and regain institutional leverage. Theirs is broader than opposition to Trump. They campaigned on affordability – housing, prices, healthcare, and energy – while presenting themselves as the party prepared to check executive excesses. Their challenge was to turn anger into a governing argument, not merely a protest vote. The parties were not evenly matched in mood. Polling and early voting data indicated strong Democratic enthusiasm. Compared with Republicans, Democrats seemed far more motivated to vote, a sign that opposition to Trump brought infrequent voters to the polls – something party leaders had not succeeded at. Moreover, Trump’s claims on the economy, as with every other claim, became contested territory. Bloomberg reported that his handling of the economy, alongside the war in Iran, contributed to his very low approval ratings. Immigration was another defining issue. For Trump’s base, border enforcement is a promise kept. For Democrats and many independents, the obvious fact is that enforcement has become murderous, indiscriminate, divisive and damaging to America’s image. For young, minority and urban voters, immigration is a moral and civil-rights question. Foreign policy was another layer. The war in Iran has turned national security from a Republican talking point into a subject of scrutiny. Voters may support a strong military, but they also ask what a war would cost, who would fight it, and whether it would make everyday life safer. Americans showed up even with protest votes. Early voting data showed that roughly 54 million Americans had already cast ballots before election day. Of those, about 43 per cent were Democrats, 32 per cent were Republicans, and 25 per cent were independents or unaffiliated voters. More striking is the reported increase in turnout among voters of colour in the states that release race and ethnicity data. That matters because Democrats made gains among young, non-white and previously disengaged voters – groups that traditionally turn out at lower rates in midterms. The election was not decided in California or New York, where outcomes are largely predictable. It was decided in a handful of competitive states and districts: North Carolina, Georgia, Maine, Michigan, Texas, Ohio and Alaska were among the key battlegrounds. Now with Democrats in control of Congress, Trump’s final two years could change. For example, the Democratic Congress can investigate administration decisions, subpoena officials, scrutinise spending, examine the conduct of the war in Iran, and challenge policies on immigration, healthcare and the economy. The days of a rubber-stamp Congress may be well and truly over, and tougher scrutiny may be expected. Yet, while winning Congress gives Democrats substantial power to investigate, block new legislation and bargain over funding, it does not necessarily give them the votes to dismantle Trump’s existing legislative programmes while he remains president. Controversial Trump-signed laws, such as the tax-and-spending law in 2025 (the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill), the mandatory immigration detention for certain non-citizens charged with specified offences (the Laken Riley Act 2025), and federal judicial appointments, will be harder to reverse than imagined. Underestimate a demagogue at your peril. Trump may well rule America for the rest of his term by veto and Executive Orders, without Congress. It remains to be seen if, finally, the midterm has taught the Trump White House the lesson that it failed to learn from turning the world on its head. The pendulum is swinging back to the middle, but it’s still early days to be excited. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/from-the-strait-of.body_zh: 中期选举结果再次印证了斯托肯的观点：美国政治的钟摆始终在向中间摆动，这并非违背选民的意愿，而是因为选民才使它如此。特朗普的一届任期（2017—2021年）已经足以说明问题。但民主党通过打造保姆国家、层层叠加繁文缛节并将 wokenism 奉为圭臬而迷失方向后，特朗普的特立独行反倒显得像是中间路线。尽管他傲慢自负，他仍在2024年再次当选。两年后，钟摆又开始向左摆动。颇有意思的是，这位把美国拖入一场毫无必要的中东战争、给世界经济造成严重后果，挑起全球关税战，将移民刑事化，并欺凌邻国和盟国的总统，竟无法挽救自己的政党免遭选举惨败。选民刚刚提醒他，自1776年以来入主白宫的45位总统都是房客，而不是自有自住的业主。如果由他做主，特朗普会往选票箱里塞东西、制造危机，或编造任何花招来改变结果。然而，尽管他蔑视程序、心怀报复且狭隘偏执、急于雪耻，最终还是无法得逞。11月3日，绝望的选民制服了他。美国人，或者至少相当一部分美国人，已经就特朗普第二任期作出首次全国性裁决。中期选举并非总统选举，但这一次几乎具有总统选举的性质——总统巴拉克·奥巴马和特朗普本人亲自巡回各州站台造势。结果是一场民主党大突破，颇似压倒性胜利。众议院全部435个席位、参议院100个席位中的35席以及36个州长职位均接受选举。利害关系很简单：共和党此前控制国会两院。计票结束后，民主党把原本属于共和党的国会翻转为蓝色。这场较量不只是两党之间的竞争，也是两个版本的美国之间的较量——一个被特朗普的“MAGA”迷思所激励，另一个则对生活成本、特朗普滥用和滥用权力，以及美国梦缓慢瓦解深感不安。按照一条不成文的规则，中期选举往往会惩罚总统所属政党。选民把白宫钥匙交给总统后，两年后便会回来肯定或谴责现状。自特朗普第二任期开启以来，局势不仅危险，更攸关生死。美国人在街头被美国移民与海关执法局（ICE）特工枪击，这显然是国家纵容的谋杀；对伊尔汗·奥马尔等批评者的报复性攻击也令此次选举具有异乎寻常的紧迫性。特朗普亲自领衔共和党的竞选活动，要求选民假定他本人也在选票上。这清楚表明，尽管他桀骜难驯，却因可能遭受不利裁决而不安——而他确实遭遇了这一裁决。他告诉美国人假装自己就在选票上（遭遇惨败后他改口否认），并承诺若共和党获胜，每张选票将获得慷慨的5,000美元贿赂。据报道，他的寡头盟友埃隆·马斯克投入了4.74亿美元。然而，特朗普仍受到惩罚，共和党败选。他的支持率接近历史低点，公众的不满集中于经济以及在伊朗打的那场愚蠢战争。共和党国会从未觉得有紧迫感去处理这场战争，却又束手无策地无法阻止。选举结果证明，特朗普一直是白宫的负担和一次政治误判，因为共和党候选人竭力与这位要求忠诚、极少认错的总统划清界限。他们仍是特朗普的帮凶，他们的失败不值得哀悼。对民主党而言，这次选举令人耳目一新，也提供了重建并重获制度影响力的机会。民主党的立场远不只是反对特朗普。他们围绕生活可负担性展开竞选——住房、物价、医疗和能源——同时把自己塑造成准备制衡行政权力越界的政党。他们面临的挑战，是把愤怒转化为治国理据，而不只是投一张抗议票。两党的情绪基础并不同等。民调和提前投票数据显示，民主党热情高涨。与共和党相比，民主党选民似乎更有投票动力，这表明反对特朗普促使那些不常投票的人走进投票站，而这是党内领导人此前未能做到的。此外，特朗普对经济的说法，和他的其他所有说法一样，也成为争议地带。彭博社报道称，他对经济的处理以及伊朗战争共同导致了他的支持率极低。移民是另一个决定性议题。对特朗普的基本盘而言，边境执法是已经兑现的承诺。对民主党和许多独立选民而言，显而易见的事实是，执法已经变得杀戮化、缺乏选择性、具有分裂性，并损害了美国形象。对年轻选民、少数族裔选民和城市选民而言，移民是道德和公民权利问题。外交政策是另一层因素。伊朗战争已把国家安全从共和党的宣传口号变成受审视的议题。选民或许支持强大的军队，但也会追问战争要付出什么代价、谁来参战，以及它能否让日常生活更安全。美国人即使投的是抗议票，也出来投票了。提前投票数据显示，约有5,400万美国人在选举日之前已经投票。其中，约43%是民主党人，32%是共和党人，25%是独立选民或无党派选民。更引人注目的是，据报道，在公布种族和族裔数据的州，有色人种选民的投票率有所上升。这一点很重要，因为民主党在年轻选民、非白人选民和此前政治疏离选民中取得了进展，而这些群体在中选举中的传统投票率较低。决定此次选举胜负的并非结果大体可预测的加利福尼亚州或纽约州，而是少数竞争激烈的州和选区：北卡罗来纳州、佐治亚州、缅因州、密歇根州、得克萨斯州、俄亥俄州和阿拉斯加州均属关键战场。如今民主党掌控国会，特朗普最后两年的处境可能会改变。例如，民主党国会可以调查政府的决策、传唤官员、审查开支、检查伊朗战争的行为，并挑战移民、医疗和经济方面的政策。橡皮图章式国会的日子或许真的结束了，更严格的监督可以预期。然而，赢得国会虽然赋予民主党相当大的权力，可以展开调查、阻止新立法并围绕拨款进行谈判，却不一定会让他们在特朗普仍是总统时获得足够的票数来推翻他现有的立法计划。由特朗普签署的争议性法律，例如2025年的税收与支出法（所谓《一项宏大而美好的法案》）、对被控犯有特定罪行的某些非公民实行强制拘留的《莱肯·赖利法案2025》，以及联邦司法任命，推翻难度将超出人们的想象。低估煽动者必然后悔。特朗普完全可能凭借否决权和行政命令，在没有国会的情况下继续主导美国余下的任期。中期选举是否终于教会了特朗普白宫从把世界掀翻这件事中未能吸取的教训，仍有待观察。钟摆正在摆回中间，但现在还远不到兴奋的时候。我们占了上风。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角，直接送达你的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入 https://dailytrust.com/muslim-candidates.body: Muslim candidates made history in Tuesday’s US midterm elections, winning seats in Congress and state legislatures despite a campaign marked by a surge in anti-Muslim rhetoric and attacks targeting their communities. The results included the election of America’s first Muslim senator, an Egyptian-American surgeon who treated wounded Palestinians in Gaza, and several Palestinian-American candidates. The victories came after President Donald Trump and his allies targeted Muslim candidates, particularly Michigan’s Abdul El-Sayed, who faced baseless allegations linking him to extremist groups. At least seven Muslim candidates were elected to Congress, including one senator and six House representatives. Egyptian-American Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, 42, defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan to become the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. A physician and public health specialist, El-Sayed campaigned on healthcare, living costs and reducing corporate influence in politics. He also criticised US military assistance to Israel and Egypt, while rejecting accusations of Muslim Brotherhood links made by political opponents. Egyptian-American surgeon Adam Hamawy defeated Republican Greg Mele in New Jersey’s 12th Congressional District, becoming the state’s first Muslim representative in Congress. A former US Army surgeon, Hamawy helped save the life of future senator Tammy Duckworth after her helicopter was shot down in Iraq in 2004. He later volunteered in Gaza, treating Palestinians wounded in Israeli attacks, including children with severe injuries. Rashida Tlaib: Palestinian-American congresswoman wins again Rashida Tlaib secured a fifth term representing Michigan’s 12th Congressional District. The Palestinian-American Democrat, one of the first two Muslim women elected to Congress in 2018, remains a prominent critic of Israel’s war on Gaza. The Somali-American Democrat, another of Congress’s first Muslim women, has repeatedly criticised US support for Israel and faced attacks from President Donald Trump. Darializa Avila Chevalier: First Latina Muslim congresswoman The 33-year-old Democrat, of Dominican heritage, was reported to have become the first Latina Muslim woman elected to Congress. She previously gained prominence through civil rights activism and pro-Palestinian protests. Two other Muslim Democrats secured re-election to the House. Andre Carson retained Indiana’s 7th District, which he has represented since 2008, while civil rights advocate Lateefah Simon won another term in California’s 12th District. Her family was displaced from Palestine in 1948, eventually settling in the United States. Kawas campaigned on affordable housing, healthcare, immigrant rights and opposition to US funding for Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza. Lebanese-American Democrat Abbas Alawieh was elected to Michigan’s 2nd State Senate District, covering Dearborn and surrounding communities. Alawieh helped establish the Uncommitted movement, which challenged former President Joe Biden’s support for Israel during the 2024 presidential election. Previously a state representative, Syed’s victory transferred the seat from Republican to Democratic control. Arab-American Republican Darin LaHood retained his Illinois congressional seat. LaHood, whose great-grandparents emigrated from Lebanon, has spoken proudly of his Lebanese heritage, saying: “I’m very proud of that heritage.” He also co-chairs the US-Lebanon Friendship Caucus and has worked to strengthen ties between Washington and Beirut. Several Palestinian-American candidates also secured victories in state legislative elections, including Iman Jodeh in Colorado’s 29th State Senate District and Ruwa Romman in Georgia’s 7th State Senate District. In Illinois, Palestinian-American Democrat Abdelnasser Rashid was projected to retain his state House seat. Other Muslim women reportedly elected included Zaynab Mohamed in Minnesota, Munira Abdullahi in Ohio, Maryam Khan in Connecticut and Madinah Wilson-Anton in Delaware. Pakistani-American lawmakers Salman Bhojani and Suleman Lalani also secured re-election in Texas, while Saud Anwar retained his Connecticut State Senate seat and Tarik Khan won another term in Pennsylvania’s House. https://dailytrust.com/muslim-candidates.title_zh: 穆斯林候选人在美国中期选举中创造历史
https://dailytrust.com/muslim-candidates.body_zh: 穆斯林候选人在周二的美国中期选举中创造了历史。尽管此次竞选充斥着反穆斯林言论激增以及针对其社区的袭击，他们仍在国会和州议会赢得了席位。选举结果包括美国首位穆斯林参议员的诞生，他是一名曾在加沙治疗受伤巴勒斯坦人的埃及裔美国外科医生，以及多名巴勒斯坦裔美国候选人的胜选。此前，总统唐纳德·特朗普及其盟友针对穆斯林候选人展开攻击，尤其是密歇根州的阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德，后者遭到毫无根据的指控，被声称与极端组织有关。至少有7名穆斯林候选人当选国会议员，其中包括1名参议员和6名众议员。42岁的埃及裔美国民主党人阿卜杜勒·埃尔-赛义德在密歇根州击败共和党人迈克·罗杰斯，成为首位当选美国参议员的穆斯林。作为一名医生和公共卫生专家，埃尔-赛义德以医疗保健、生活成本以及减少企业影响政治为竞选主题。他还批评美国对以色列和埃及的军事援助，同时驳斥政治对手关于其与穆斯林兄弟会有关联的指控。埃及裔美国外科医生亚当·哈马维在新泽西州第12国会选区击败共和党人格雷格·梅莱，成为该州首位进入国会的穆斯林代表。作为一名前美国陆军外科医生，2004年未来参议员塔米·达科沃斯的直升机在伊拉克遭击落后，哈马维曾协助挽救她的生命。此后，他自愿前往加沙，治疗在以色列袭击中受伤的巴勒斯坦人，其中包括遭受严重伤害的儿童。拉希达·特莱布：巴勒斯坦裔美国女议员再次胜选拉希达·特莱布成功赢得第五个任期，继续代表密歇根州第12国会选区。这位巴勒斯坦裔美国民主党人是2018年首批当选国会的两名穆斯林女性之一，她仍是加沙战争的主要批评者。这名索马里裔美国民主党人是国会首批穆斯林女性之一，曾多次批评美国对以色列的支持，并遭到总统唐纳德·特朗普的攻击。达里亚利萨·阿维拉·谢瓦利耶：首位拉丁裔穆斯林女议员据报道，这名33岁的民主党人拥有多米尼加裔背景，成为首位当选国会的拉丁裔穆斯林女性。她此前因参与民权行动和声援巴勒斯坦示威而广受关注。另有两名穆斯林民主党人成功赢得众议员连任。安德烈·卡森守住了印第安纳州第7选区，他自2008年以来一直代表该选区；民权活动家Lateefah Simon则在加利福尼亚州第12选区再次赢得一个任期。她的家人在1948年被迫离开巴勒斯坦，后来最终在美国定居。卡瓦斯以可负担住房、医疗保健、移民权利以及反对美国资助以色列在加沙实施的种族灭绝战争为竞选主题。黎巴嫩裔美国民主党人阿巴斯·阿拉维赫当选密歇根州第2州参议院选区议员，该选区覆盖迪尔伯恩及周边社区。阿拉维赫曾协助建立“不承诺”运动，在2024年总统选举期间挑战前总统乔·拜登对以色列的支持。阿拉维赫此前担任州众议员，赛义德的胜选使该席位由共和党掌控转为民主党掌控。阿拉伯裔美国共和党人达林·拉胡德守住了他在伊利诺伊州的国会席位。拉胡德的曾祖父母来自黎巴嫩，他曾自豪地谈及自己的黎巴嫩血统，并表示：“我为这份血统深感自豪。”他还共同主持美国—黎巴嫩友好小组，并努力加强华盛顿与贝鲁特之间的联系。数名巴勒斯坦裔美国候选人也在州议会选举中获胜，包括科罗拉多州第29州参议院选区的伊曼·乔德和佐治亚州第7州参议院选区的鲁瓦·罗曼。在伊利诺伊州，巴勒斯坦裔美国民主党人阿卜杜勒-纳赛尔·拉希德预计将保住其州众议员席位。据报道，其他当选的穆斯林女性还包括明尼苏达州的泽纳布·穆罕默德、俄亥俄州的穆妮拉·阿卜杜拉希、康涅狄格州的玛丽亚姆·汗，以及特拉华州的马迪娜·威尔逊-安东尼。巴基斯坦裔美国议员萨尔曼·博贾尼和苏莱曼·拉拉尼也在得克萨斯州成功连任；绍德·阿马尔守住了康涅狄格州参议院席位，塔里克·汗则在宾夕法尼亚州众议院再次赢得一个任期。加入《每日信任》WhatsApp社群，快速获取身边新闻与动态

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body: SEATTLE — Democrats' sweeping victories in Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections brought relief to many Koreans frustrated with President Donald Trump, but that relief did not necessarily translate into support for the Democratic Party. That was how Bo Young Lee, a Korean American business executive, summed up the election results. "Ultimately, the results on Tuesday were a byproduct of citizens' frustration with the Trump administration, rising costs, and the attacks on democracy," Lee, an international speaker specializing in AI ethics and corporate diversity, told The Korea Times. Another Korean American voter, a 47-year-old Texas resident who has traditionally supported Republicans, said she crossed party lines for the first time in Tuesday's election. "I voted Democratic simply because I wanted anyone but the Republicans," she said, requesting anonymity. "It was the first time in my life I'd ever voted for a Democrat." Her decision came as Texas, long considered a Republican stronghold, delivered some of the election's biggest surprises. Democrats won the governorship and a U.S. Senate seat in the state for the first time in decades, marking a dramatic shift in a state that had consistently rejected Democratic candidates in statewide races. The Democratic victories dealt a major setback to Trump, giving the party control of both chambers of Congress and setting the stage for a divided government during the remaining two years of his presidency. Across Korean-language online communities, the results prompted everything from celebrations to expressions of disbelief and cautious optimism. "I've lived in the U.S. for 20 years, and this is the first time I've paid so much attention to a midterm election," one commenter wrote. "I thought America had no hope after Trump became president for a second time. Now I feel a little reassured. At least there will be some checks on Trump's unchecked power." Another commenter said the results brought tears, describing the comfort of realizing that many others shared the same frustrations. Yet the conversations also showed that opposition to Trump did not necessarily translate into support for Democrats. One California resident said they had traditionally voted Republican because of disagreements with Democratic policies but voted Democratic this time out of frustration with Trump. "I absolutely despise Trump, but I don't support Democrats either because I disagree with many of their policies," one person wrote. Much of the debate centered on everyday concerns rather than party loyalty. Some blamed Trump's tariffs and economic policies for worsening the cost of living. Others worried that Democratic policies would increase government spending and place greater burdens on middle-class families. Education also emerged as a contentious issue, particularly among parents discussing LGBTQ-related topics in schools. Some expressed concerns about what their children were being taught, while others pushed back against what they considered exaggerated fears. The contrasting views highlighted differing political views among Korean Americans, with some putting aside longstanding party loyalties to oppose Trump while others remained skeptical of Democratic policies. Lee said the results reflected broader dissatisfaction with the Trump administration, but warned that Democrats should not take their victories for granted. "The newly elected Democrats can't forget the frustration that swept them into office. If people don't see meaningful change within a short period, we may see different results in 2028," she said
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.title_zh: 旅美韩国人欢迎民主党取得胜利，但对未来走向仍存疑虑
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/world/20261.body_zh: 西雅图——民主党在周二举行的美国中期选举中取得压倒性胜利，这让许多对唐纳德·特朗普总统感到失望的韩国人如释重负，但这种宽慰未必转化为对民主党的支持。旅美韩裔企业高管Bo Young Lee正是这样总结此次选举结果的。李在接受《韩国时报》采访时说：“归根结底，周二的结果是公民对特朗普政府的不满、生活成本上涨以及针对民主制度的攻击共同造成的副产品。”李是一名专注于人工智能伦理和企业多元化的国际演讲者。另一名旅美韩裔选民是一名47岁的得克萨斯州居民，过去一直支持共和党；她说，周二这次选举是她首次跨党派投票。“我投票给民主党，只是因为除了共和党之外，我愿意支持任何人。”她表示，并要求匿名。“这是我有生以来第一次投票给民主党人。”她的决定出现在得克萨斯州出人意料的选举结果之中。长期以来，得克萨斯州一直被视为共和党的大本营，但在此次选举中，民主党数十年来首次赢得该州州长职位和一个美国联邦参议院席位，这在该州全州范围的选举中历来拒绝民主党候选人的背景下，标志着一场剧烈转变。民主党的胜利对特朗普构成重大打击，使该党掌控了国会两院，并为特朗普剩余两年任期内的分立政府局面铺路。在韩语网络社群中，选举结果引发了庆祝、难以置信和谨慎乐观等不同反应。一名评论者写道：“我在美国生活了20年，这是第一次如此关注中期选举。我原以为特朗普第二任期开始后，美国就毫无希望了。现在我感到稍微安心了一些。至少会对特朗普不受制约的权力形成一些制衡。”另一名评论者说，选举结果令她感动落泪，因为意识到许多人也怀着同样的不满。然而，讨论也表明，反特朗普并不一定会转化为支持民主党。一名加利福尼亚州居民说，由于与民主党政策存在分歧，他过去一直投票给共和党，但此次出于对特朗普的不满而投票给民主党。一人写道：“我非常厌恶特朗普，但也不支持民主党，因为他们许多政策都与我相左。”争论大多围绕日常生活问题，而非党派忠诚。一些人将生活成本恶化归咎于特朗普的关税和经济政策。另一些人担心，民主党的政策会增加政府支出，给中产家庭带来更沉重的负担。教育也成为一个有争议的话题，尤其是在讨论学校 LGBTQ相关议题的家长之中。一些人担忧孩子正在接受的教育内容，另一些人则反驳他们认为被夸大的恐惧。这些对立观点凸显了韩裔美国人之间不同的政治立场：一些人搁置长期以来的党派忠诚，以反对特朗普；另一些人则仍对民主党政策持怀疑态度。李表示，选举结果反映了人们对特朗普政府更广泛的不满，但警告民主党不应把胜利视为理所当然。她说：“新当选的民主党人不能忘记，正是这股不满情绪把他们推上了台。如果人们短期内看不到有意义的改变，那么2028年我们可能会看到不同的结果。”
